note: WAEC Marketing round 8 (R45 top-up): generic brand; individual brand; quality control; testimonial; infomercial; outdoor advertising; exhibition; showroom; cash on delivery; order cycle; shelf space; planogram; supply chain; third-party logistics; cross-docking; haggling; seasonal discount; instalment buying; pay per click; e-tailing; value for money; sales contest; sales analysis; marketing budget; multichannel. Scanned against the whole Marketing pool (WAEC and NECO stems).

questions.subject: Marketing
questions.q: Products that carry no brand name at all and are known only by the name of the product class itself, such as plain sachets labelled simply 'salt', are
questions.explanation: No name distinguishes them but their price.

questions.subject: Marketing
questions.q: A soap maker gives each of its products a separate name — Joy for bathing soap, Spark for washing soap — instead of one family name. This naming policy is
questions.explanation: Every product stands or falls on its own name.

questions.subject: Marketing
questions.q: The checks a firm carries out at every stage of production so that every unit leaving the factory meets the standard set for it are called
questions.explanation: Bad units are caught before they ship out.

questions.subject: Marketing
questions.q: A satisfied customer appears in a television advert saying how a cough mixture cured her cough. Her statement in the advert is a
questions.explanation: A real user's own words vouch for the goods.

questions.subject: Marketing
questions.q: A paid television programme that may last half an hour, demonstrating a blender or a fitness machine and giving a phone number to order from, is called an
questions.explanation: It is half information and half commercial.

questions.subject: Marketing
questions.q: Advertising done on poster sites, painted walls, bus shelters and street furniture, where people see it as they move about outdoors, is known as
questions.explanation: The message waits for passers-by on the streets.

questions.subject: Marketing
questions.q: An event at which many firms gather under one roof, each at its own stand, to display their goods and meet customers face to face, is an
questions.explanation: Buyers walk from stand to stand all day.

questions.subject: Marketing
questions.q: A room in the dealer's premises where products are neatly arranged and lit so that customers can examine them before buying is a
questions.explanation: The goods are displayed, not hidden in cartons.

questions.subject: Marketing
questions.q: A shopper pays for his groceries only when the supermarket's rider delivers them to his door. This method of payment is
questions.explanation: Money changes hands only as the goods arrive.

questions.subject: Marketing
questions.q: The period of time between one order a customer places and the next order he places for the same goods is called the
questions.explanation: The clock restarts each time he reorders.

questions.subject: Marketing
questions.q: A toothpaste maker notices its brand is losing shelf space to rivals in the big stores. The phrase 'shelf space' refers to
questions.B: the size of the factory floor
questions.C: the room a product occupies on a shelf
questions.explanation: More room on the shelf means more chance to sell.

questions.subject: Marketing
questions.q: The diagram a retailer uses to show exactly where every product should sit on each shelf, so that every branch is laid out the same way, is a
questions.explanation: Even a new shop assistant can stock the shelf right.

questions.subject: Marketing
questions.q: The whole network of suppliers, producers, warehouses, transporters and sellers through which a product travels from raw material to the final consumer is the
questions.explanation: Every link must hold for the goods to arrive.

questions.subject: Marketing
questions.q: A manufacturing firm hands over its storage and delivery work entirely to a specialist company that does nothing but move other firms' goods. This arrangement is
questions.explanation: Another firm's trucks now carry the burden.

questions.subject: Marketing
questions.q: At a distribution centre, goods are unloaded from one truck and straight into another for onward delivery, without ever being put into store. This practice is
questions.explanation: The goods barely touch the ground as they pass.

questions.subject: Marketing
questions.q: At Tejuosho market, a buyer and a seller argue back and forth over the price of a pair of shoes until they agree on one. This negotiation is called
questions.explanation: The final price is settled by argument.

questions.subject: Marketing
questions.q: At the end of the rainy season a clothing store cuts the price of its raincoats heavily to clear them before the dry season. This price cut is a
questions.explanation: The time of year dictates the reduction.

questions.subject: Marketing
questions.q: A trader allows a customer to take a refrigerator home at once and pay the price in small monthly amounts until it is complete. This arrangement is
questions.explanation: The payment arrives piece by piece.

questions.subject: Marketing
questions.q: In online advertising, the arrangement in which the advertiser pays the website a small sum every single time a visitor clicks on the advert is
questions.explanation: No click, no charge for that visitor.

questions.subject: Marketing
questions.q: The business of selling goods to final consumers directly over the internet, through a shop's own website or app, is called
questions.explanation: The shop counter is now a screen.

questions.subject: Marketing
questions.q: A buyer looks at a torch, weighs its price against how long it will last and how well it will serve him, and concludes it is worth buying. His judgement is about the torch's
questions.explanation: Is the price fair for what the thing does?

questions.subject: Marketing
questions.q: A firm offers its salesmen a weekend in Dubai for whoever sells the most units in the month. This incentive device is a
questions.explanation: The best seller takes the prize.

questions.subject: Marketing
questions.q: The marketing staff sit down at month's end to study their sales figures product by product and zone by zone, to see what is moving and what is not. This study is a
questions.explanation: The figures themselves tell the story.

questions.subject: Marketing
questions.q: The statement of money a firm sets aside and plans to spend on advertising, promotion and research during the coming year is its
questions.explanation: It caps what the department may spend.

questions.subject: Marketing
questions.q: A bookshop now sells through its physical shop, its website and its phone app all at once. This approach is
questions.explanation: The customer chooses how to buy.
